Reuse settings and export an auditable analysis

Source: vignettes/recipes-and-exports.Rmd
recipes-and-exports.Rmd

A recipe preserves calculation settings. An analysis record also preserves original texts, counted units, unavailable results, document metadata and the calculation environment. You can reuse settings on another folder, inspect differences between runs and describe what was actually calculated. This does not decide whether two study populations are comparable.

The initial recipe schema supports raw text, surface forms and all word tokens, with either built-in tokenizer and optional pinned NJ8/TUBELEX references. Lemma/flemma reconstruction, custom resources and external annotation pipelines continue to use the existing APIs and complete RDS records. Their settings are not inferred from partially recorded metadata.

Define and reuse settings 

plan <- lexdiv_plan(presets = character(), specs = list(
  lexdiv_spec("ttr"),
  lexdiv_spec("mattr", list(window_length = 5), request_id = "mattr5"),
  lexdiv_spec("mtld", list(threshold = 0.72))))
recipe <- lexdiv_recipe(plan, normalization = "NFC", case = "lower")
texts <- c("001" = "A small cat watches another small cat near the window.",
           "002" = "Writers revise their texts and retain earlier drafts.",
           "003" = "")
metadata <- data.frame(document_id = names(texts),
  writer_id = c("w1", "w1", "w2"), task = "description", occasion = c(1, 2, 1))
run <- lexdiv_run_recipe(texts, recipe, metadata = metadata, condition_id = "primary")
run$analysis$results[, c("document_id", "request_id", "value", "status", "missing_reason")]
#> <lexdiv_profile_batch_results: 3 documents; 9 specification results; schema unknown>
#>   document_id                            request_id      value  status
#> 1         001  ttr-4fb55d484c9910369ed7bfb8e1bb1631  0.8000000      ok
#> 2         001                                mattr5  0.9333333      ok
#> 3         001 mtld-f3c9dc19ce5334b9bd2c0d537d29daac 12.0000000      ok
#> 4         002  ttr-4fb55d484c9910369ed7bfb8e1bb1631  1.0000000      ok
#> 5         002                                mattr5  1.0000000      ok
#> 6         002 mtld-f3c9dc19ce5334b9bd2c0d537d29daac         NA missing
#> 7         003  ttr-4fb55d484c9910369ed7bfb8e1bb1631         NA missing
#> 8         003                                mattr5         NA missing
#> 9         003 mtld-f3c9dc19ce5334b9bd2c0d537d29daac         NA missing
#>   missing_reason
#> 1           <NA>
#> 2           <NA>
#> 3           <NA>
#> 4           <NA>
#> 5           <NA>
#> 6      no_factor
#> 7    empty_input
#> 8    empty_input
#> 9    empty_input

The two documents by w1 remain linked. Three documents and several measures do not become independent writer observations. The saved $analysis retains the complete batch result accepted by lexdiv_study_table().

Presets are expanded before saving. Reading does not substitute today’s defaults. Execution requires the recorded package, method/preprocessing contracts, tokenizer, stringi and ICU versions. To deliberately change environments, construct a new recipe and retain the original. Reusing a recipe restores settings; reproducing a result also requires identical source texts.

folder <- tempfile("ldfreq-example-")
dir.create(folder)
lexdiv_write(recipe, file.path(folder, "recipe.json"))
lexdiv_write(run, file.path(folder, "analysis.json"))
restored <- lexdiv_read(file.path(folder, "analysis.json"))
stopifnot(identical(restored, run))
repeated <- lexdiv_run_recipe(texts,
  lexdiv_read(file.path(folder, "recipe.json")), metadata = metadata)
stopifnot(identical(repeated$analysis$results, run$analysis$results))

Recipes contain no source texts. Analysis JSON contains source texts and token audits: keep it under the study’s access rules. Existing files are never overwritten. Factor and date/time metadata become character labels in this portable record; retain original R objects if their classes or levels are needed.

Keep the study’s planned observations separately from the submitted documents. Here w2 submitted an empty text at the first occasion and no text at the second:

planned <- data.frame(observation_id = paste0("o", 1:4),
  writer_id = c("w1", "w1", "w2", "w2"), task = factor("description"),
  occasion = c(1, 2, 1, 2))
submissions <- data.frame(observation_id = paste0("o", 1:3),
  document_id = restored$documents$document_id)
study <- lexdiv_study_table(planned, submissions, restored$analysis, plan,
  condition_id = restored$condition_id)
study[, c("observation_id", "writer_id", "occasion", "request_id", "input_status")]
#>    observation_id writer_id occasion                            request_id
#> 1              o1        w1        1  ttr-4fb55d484c9910369ed7bfb8e1bb1631
#> 2              o1        w1        1                                mattr5
#> 3              o1        w1        1 mtld-f3c9dc19ce5334b9bd2c0d537d29daac
#> 4              o2        w1        2  ttr-4fb55d484c9910369ed7bfb8e1bb1631
#> 5              o2        w1        2                                mattr5
#> 6              o2        w1        2 mtld-f3c9dc19ce5334b9bd2c0d537d29daac
#> 7              o3        w2        1  ttr-4fb55d484c9910369ed7bfb8e1bb1631
#> 8              o3        w2        1                                mattr5
#> 9              o3        w2        1 mtld-f3c9dc19ce5334b9bd2c0d537d29daac
#> 10             o4        w2        2  ttr-4fb55d484c9910369ed7bfb8e1bb1631
#> 11             o4        w2        2                                mattr5
#> 12             o4        w2        2 mtld-f3c9dc19ce5334b9bd2c0d537d29daac
#>       input_status
#> 1  selected_tokens
#> 2  selected_tokens
#> 3  selected_tokens
#> 4  selected_tokens
#> 5  selected_tokens
#> 6  selected_tokens
#> 7       empty_text
#> 8       empty_text
#> 9       empty_text
#> 10   not_submitted
#> 11   not_submitted
#> 12   not_submitted

This retains four planned observations, three submitted documents and their distinct missingness states. Use lexdiv_study_model_data() to select a single response after making reporting decisions. The planned table retains its R types and factor levels; save it and the study table as RDS alongside the JSON.

Inspect differences 

other <- lexdiv_run_recipe(c(other = "A different text."), recipe)
comparison <- lexdiv_compare_analyses(run, other)
comparison$measurement
#> [1] "same"
comparison$differences
#>                   field severity
#> 1 selected_token_counts  caution
#> 2          availability  caution
#>                                                       left
#> 1                                                 [0,8,10]
#> 2 {"documents":3,"unavailable":4,"below_advisory_floor":7}
#>                                                      right
#> 1                                                        3
#> 2 {"documents":1,"unavailable":2,"below_advisory_floor":2}
#>                                                                                                      explanation
#> 1 Document counts or length distributions differ. Evaluate length sensitivity for each measure and study design.
#> 2                       Availability or advisory-length flags differ; flags do not automatically exclude scores.

measurement = "same" means no recorded measurement-definition, preprocessing engine or resource-setting difference was found. Package-version changes are separate cautions: review release changes before treating implementations as equivalent. study_comparability remains "not_established". Task, sampling, genre, writer dependencies and uncertainty require the study’s own analysis. Length/coverage differences do not impose a universal exclusion cutoff. Lengths are checked both as a batch distribution and by shared document ID. Swapped lengths therefore produce a caution even when the distributions match. A shared ID does not by itself establish that two rows are paired observations.

Different windows or resources may be intentional sensitivity conditions. The checker identifies different measurements and preserves both runs; it does not forbid that question or pool the scores. Unknown schemas, incomplete request rows and inconsistent source/count records are rejected.

Write methods text and tidy CSV 

cat(lexdiv_methods_text(run, "en"), sep = "\n\n")
#> Lexical diversity was calculated for 3 documents using ldfreq 1.0.0.9001. Tokenization used ldfreq-english-word-tokenizer (version 0.1.0), NFC Unicode normalization, case handling 'lower', and exclusion of numeric tokens. Surface forms were analyzed without content-word filtering. Normalization used stringi 1.8.9 (ICU 74.2).
#> 
#> We calculated Type-token ratio (V / N). Method ID: ttr_v_over_n_v1. Parameters: none.
#> 
#> We calculated Moving-average TTR (mean TTR of all step-one overlapping windows). Method ID: mattr_sliding_step1_v1. Parameters: window_length = 5.
#> 
#> We calculated Measure of textual lexical diversity (mean forward/reverse tokens per factor; strict <, no minimum length with final-token closure checks, residual credit (1 - TTR) / (1 - threshold), and the arithmetic mean of directional scores). Method ID: mtld_seq_bidir_dirmean_lt_nomin_linear_tail_v1. Parameters: threshold = 0.72.
#> 
#> Of 9 document-by-specification rows, 4 were non-computable and retained with their missingness reasons. Advisory length flags did not automatically exclude scores. Matching settings and computability do not establish measurement precision or study comparability.
#> 
#> References:
#> Komuro, R. (2026). ldfreq: Reproducible Lexical Diversity and Frequency Profiles. R package version 1.0.0.9001.
#> Covington, M. A., & McFall, J. D. (2010). Cutting the Gordian Knot: The Moving-Average Type-Token Ratio (MATTR). https://doi.org/10.1080/09296171003643098
#> McCarthy, P. M., & Jarvis, S. (2010). MTLD, vocd-D, and HD-D: A validation study of sophisticated approaches to lexical diversity assessment. https://doi.org/10.3758/BRM.42.2.381

Use lexdiv_methods_text(run, "ja") for Japanese. Both languages retain the calculation version, including the saved stringi and ICU normalization versions. Numeric parameters use a decimal point even if R’s OutDec option is a comma. Parameters, MTLD closure/tail rules, unavailable rows and resource lookup choices are explicit. References cover software, MATTR, MTLD/HD-D and used resources. Other methods retain their precise definitions and IDs; review and add literature needed for the paper’s substantive claims. Supply your sampling description, setting rationale and inferential methods.

lexdiv_write(run, file.path(folder, "results.csv"), format = "csv")
flat <- read.csv(file.path(folder, "results.csv"),
  colClasses = c(document_id = "character", missing_reason = "character"),
  na.strings = "", encoding = "UTF-8")
stopifnot(identical(flat$document_id, run$analysis$results$document_id),
  isTRUE(all.equal(flat$value, run$analysis$results$value)))

Each row is a document x condition x measurement request. Two MATTR windows retain distinct requests. Missing values/reasons survive; parameter/diagnostic list columns become JSON strings. Explicit character types retain leading zeros in CSV IDs. Keep JSON beside CSV: preprocessing, resource profiles and metadata remain in the complete record rather than being discarded or flattened into misleading repeated observations.

Optional references 

lexdiv_resource_info(c("nj8", "tubelex"))
# After reviewing terms and explicitly obtaining the pinned resources:
reference_recipe <- lexdiv_recipe(plan, resources = c("nj8", "tubelex"),
  tubelex_tokenization_mismatch = "allow")
reference_run <- lexdiv_run_recipe(texts, reference_recipe)
reference_run$profiles$nj8$coverage
reference_run$profiles$tubelex$summary
nj8_diagnostics(reference_run$profiles$nj8)
tubelex_diagnostics(reference_run$profiles$tubelex)
# These same diagnostics and plot(reference_run$profiles$tubelex) also work
# after lexdiv_write() followed by lexdiv_read().

NJ8 uses surface forms, NFKC/lowercase lookup and parenthetical aliases; off-list forms remain in the denominator. The built-in tokenizer differs from TUBELEX’s Treebank segmentation, so explicit "allow" records a segmentation-sensitivity analysis. Coverage does not establish alignment. Missing/modified caches stop execution; there is no automatic download or resource substitution.

Terminal and Python entry points

Locate the installed CLI with system.file("exec", "ldfreq.R", package = "ldfreq"):

Rscript /path/to/ldfreq/exec/ldfreq.R --init recipe.json
Rscript /path/to/ldfreq/exec/ldfreq.R --recipe recipe.json --input texts --output new-results

UTF-8 .txt files, including empty files, are read in sorted relative-path order. Add --recursive for subfolders; relative paths are document IDs. The new output folder contains recipe/analysis JSON, metric CSV and both methods texts. Failures return nonzero status without publishing a partial output folder. Existing output folders are refused.

Add the installed directory returned by system.file("python", package = "ldfreq") to Python’s module path:

import ldfreq_r
recipe = ldfreq_r.default_recipe()
result = ldfreq_r.analyze_text("A short example text.", recipe)
batch = ldfreq_r.analyze_folder("texts", "recipe.json", output="python-results")

Python uses only its standard library and invokes the installed R CLI. R and R’s jsonlite are required. The returned dictionary is the CLI’s JSON: tables contain table_schema, types and column arrays under data. Typed vectors retain empty arrays, missing values and binary64 numbers.

The separate Python/Web UI package named ldfreq uses its own analysis engine and aggregate-only export schema. Its exports omit source text, filenames and token-level data and round finite numbers to 12 decimal places. Its ASCII word tokenizer also differs from the R tokenizers. These records therefore cannot be treated as interchangeable with the R recipe schema. ldfreq_r leaves that Python package’s imports and behavior intact. For the Web UI schema, use the Web UI’s JSON exporter. A native folder CLI and ldfreq.cli.analyze_folder() are developed in that separate Python project; they require a distribution of that project containing ldfreq.cli and are not installed by this R package. That workflow uses the UI analysis service and JSON exporter, with the same aggregate-only retention policy; its settings must match the UI run.
